key_insight: Introducing spanwise mean-flow skew into a turbulent mixing layer changes the magnitudes of mean and turbulent quantities by up to about 40%, but leaves the layer’s core self-similar dynamics largely intact.
engineering_relevance: For 3D shear flows in aerospace, propulsion, and mixing devices, mean-flow skew should be treated as a quantitative modifier of performance rather than a fundamental change in mixing-layer behavior.
method: Added skew using turning vanes near a splitter-plate trailing edge.
Measured downstream flow evolution with cross-wire anemometry.
Compared planar and skewed configurations using similarity scaling and Reynolds-stress profiles.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports systematic reductions in mean and turbulent quantities of roughly 40% in the skewed case, while key similarity features and Townsend’s structure parameter remained approximately unchanged.
watch_item: The setup is experimentally controlled, but the findings come from a specific free-shear configuration, so transfer to other 3D turbulent flows may require revalidation.
paper_title: Effects of mean flow skew on turbulent shear layers. Part II. Experimental investigation
